statement: For taxable years beginning in 2025, the AMT exemption amounts under § 55(d)(1) are $137,000 (joint returns/surviving spouses), $88,100 (unmarried individuals), $68,500 (married filing separately), and $30,700 (estates and trusts); the exemption phases out above threshold AMTI of $1,252,700 (joint; completely phased out at $1,800,700), $626,350 (unmarried; complete at $978,750), $626,350 (MFS; complete at $900,350), and $102,500 (estates/trusts; complete at $225,300); and the 28% rate applies to excess taxable income above $239,100 ($119,550 MFS), with 26% below (Rev. Proc. 2024-40 § 2.11, applying § 55(b)(1) and § 55(d)).
caveat: 2025 amounts only — these adjust annually for inflation and the later year's revenue procedure controls later years; the complete-phaseout figures confirm the 25-cents-per-dollar phaseout arithmetic (threshold + exemption/0.25). Any use of these figures is an illustration, never a filing computation.
